candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — contraindications/adverse cardiac effects
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize QT prolongation as a major ziprasidone safety concern and identify a history of cardiac arrhythmias as a reason the medication should be avoided.

options.A: Ziprasidone can prolong the QT interval and should be avoided in clients with a history of cardiac arrhythmias
options.B: Ziprasidone shortens the QT interval and is preferred when arrhythmias are present
options.C: Ziprasidone has no clinically relevant effect on cardiac electrical conduction
options.D: Ziprasidone is contraindicated because it invariably causes severe hypoglycemia

candidate.rationale: Current DailyMed labeling warns that ziprasidone can prolong the QT interval and states that it should be avoided in patients with congenital long QT syndrome and in patients with a history of cardiac arrhythmias. Therefore A is the best answer. B and C directly contradict the labeling, and D describes an adverse effect that is neither inevitable nor the relevant contraindication in this scenario.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Ziprasidone prolongs QT and should be avoided in patients with congenital long QT syndrome or a history of cardiac arrhythmias.
